stemMd: During DNA replication, why is a new strand synthesized in short fragments on one template?

options.label: A
options.textMd: DNA polymerase extends strands only in the 5′ to 3′ direction, while the templates are antiparallel.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Short fragments are made only from amino acids.

options.label: C
options.textMd: One template contains no complementary bases.

options.label: D
options.textMd: The two parental strands run in the same direction.

options.label: E
options.textMd: DNA polymerase cannot use nucleotides containing adenine.

explanationMd: As the replication fork opens, one template can be copied continuously toward the fork. On the oppositely oriented template, the same 5′ to 3′ polymerase activity must repeatedly begin short stretches. These Okazaki fragments are later joined to make a continuous lagging strand.

distractorRationale.e: All four DNA nucleotides are used in replication.
distractorRationale.b: The fragments are DNA, not peptides.
distractorRationale.c: Both templates can guide complementary synthesis.
